title: A registration body without a name or a valid email gives 400 invalid_request
then: Each gives 400 `invalid_request`.

title: A registered email, in any case, gives 409 email_taken
when: A second registration with the same email in another case.
then: 409 `email_taken`.

title: A registration returns 201 with the member, trimmed and in lower case
then: The 201 response has a whole-number ID, the trimmed name, the lower-case email and the join time.

title: A tool body without a name gives 400 invalid_request
then: `POST /tools` without a name, or with a blank one, gives 400 `invalid_request`.

title: Adding a tool returns 201 with an available catalog entry
then: The 201 response has the name, an empty description, `condition` `good`, `damageNote` null, `status` `available` and the time added.

title: The catalog lists every tool in ID order with its condition and status
then: `GET /tools` gives 200 with every tool in ID order, each with `condition`, `damageNote` and `status`.

title: The catalog shows a tool on_loan while lent, and available after a good return
then: The tool shows `on_loan` while lent and `available` after a return in good condition.

title: An unknown member or tool gives 404 member_not_found or tool_not_found
then: An unknown member gives 404 `member_not_found`; an unknown tool gives 404 `tool_not_found`.

title: A borrow with a missing or malformed ID gives 400 invalid_request
then: `POST /loans` with no `memberId`, a `toolId` of 0, an ID sent as a string, or an ID that is not whole gives 400 `invalid_request`.

title: A member who cannot borrow gives 409 member_overdue or loan_limit_reached
then: A member with 3 loans gets 409 `loan_limit_reached`. A member can still borrow at 23:59 on a loan's due date in New York, and gets 409 `member_overdue` from 00:00 the next day.

title: An unavailable tool gives 409 tool_on_loan or tool_needs_repair
then: Borrowing a tool on loan gives 409 `tool_on_loan`; borrowing a damaged tool gives 409 `tool_needs_repair`.

title: When several borrow checks fail, the first in order is reported
then: An invalid body with an unknown member gives `invalid_request`; an unknown member and tool give `member_not_found`; a member who is both overdue and at the loan limit gets `member_overdue`; a member at the limit borrowing a damaged tool gets `loan_limit_reached`; a tool both on loan and damaged gives `tool_needs_repair`.

title: A borrow returns 201 with the loan and its due date, with no due time
then: `POST /loans` gives 201 with `borrowedAt` now, `dueDate` `2026-03-16`, `returnedAt` null and no `dueAt`.

title: A return body without good or needs_repair gives 400 invalid_condition
then: A return with no condition or an unknown one gives 400 `invalid_condition`.

title: Returning an unknown or already returned loan is refused
then: A return of an unknown loan gives 404 `loan_not_found`. A second return of a loan gives 409 `already_returned`, and changes nothing: the tool keeps the condition and note of the first return.

title: A return returns 200 with the loan and whether it was late
then: Each return gives 200 with `dueDate`, `returnedAt`, `returnCondition`, `returnNote` and `late`.

title: A damage report without a note gives 400, and for an unknown tool 404
then: Without a note gives 400 `invalid_request`; an unknown tool gives 404 `tool_not_found`.

title: A damage report returns 200 with the tool needing repair
then: 200 with `condition` `needs_repair`, `damageNote` the trimmed note and `status` `needs_repair`.

title: A damage report on a tool on loan keeps its status on_loan
then: Reporting damage on a lent tool gives `condition` `needs_repair` and `status` `on_loan`.

title: A damage report over 64 KB is refused with 413
when: Sends `POST /tools/{toolId}/damage` with a body of exactly 64 KB.
then:
Expects it to be read and the note saved. Sends one a byte over and expects 413 `body_too_large` with `Connection: close`, and the tool still `good`. Sends an over-limit body to `POST /members` and expects the same 413, so the limit holds on every endpoint's body, and the email is still free afterwards.

Then, over a raw socket, it sends a chunked damage report with no declared length that never ends, writing as fast as the connection allows. It expects a 413 `body_too_large` answer with `Connection: close`, and the server to close the connection within 5 seconds instead of waiting for the body to end.

title: Repairing an unknown tool gives 404, and a good tool 409 tool_not_damaged
then: An unknown tool gives 404 `tool_not_found`; a good tool gives 409 `tool_not_damaged`.

title: Marking a tool repaired returns 200 with it available
then: 200 with `condition` `good`, `damageNote` null and `status` `available`.
